question: The base of a right prism is an isosceles trapezium with parallel sides measuring 10 cm and 20 cm, and non-parallel sides measuring 13 cm each. The volume of the prism is 3240 cm³ . What is the total surface area of the prism?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Height of trapezium = √(13² − 5²) = 12 cm

Base area = 1/2 × (10 + 20) × 12 = 180 cm²

Prism height = Volume ÷ Base area = 3240 ÷ 180 = 18 cm

TSA = 2 × Base area + Perimeter × Prism height

TSA = 2 × 180 + (10 + 20 + 13 + 13) × 18 = 360 + 1008 = 1368 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 1368 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Parallel sides of the isosceles trapezium base, a = 10 cm, b = 20 cm

Non-parallel sides, c = 13 cm

Volume of the right prism, V = 3240 cm³

**Formula Used:**

Area of trapezium = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × Height

Volume of prism = Area of base × Height of prism

Total Surface Area of prism = 2 × (Area of base) + (Perimeter of base) × Height of prism

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/68dfa49c4b1b4a5e7223cc956d3eb33cc731f14fa509eb419faf6acd666471ba.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ The base of the right-angled triangle formed by dropping a perpendicular = (20 − 10) ÷ 2 = 5 cm

⇒ By Pythagoras theorem, height of trapezium, hₜ = √(13² − 5²) = √(169 − 25) = √144 = 12 cm

⇒ Area of trapezium base = 1/2 × (10 + 20) × 12 = 1/2 × 30 × 12 = 180 cm²

⇒ Perimeter of trapezium base = 10 + 20 + 13 + 13 = 56 cm

⇒ Volume of prism = Area of base × Height of prism

⇒ 3240 = 180 × Height of prism

⇒ Height of prism = 3240 ÷ 180 = 18 cm

⇒ Lateral Surface Area = Perimeter of base × Height of prism = 56 × 18 = 1008 cm²

⇒ Total Surface Area = 2 × Area of base + Lateral Surface Area

⇒ Total Surface Area = 2 × 180 + 1008 = 360 + 1008 = 1368 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 1368 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Prism Properties

A right prism is a 3D solid with two identical and parallel polygon bases. The lateral faces are rectangles perfectly perpendicular to the bases.

Volume of Prism

Volume is universally calculated as V = Base Area × Height. This holds true for any uniform cross-section shape.

Isosceles Trapezium

A quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides and non-parallel sides of equal length. The base angles are equal, and the diagonals are also of equal length.

Total Surface Area (TSA)

TSA of any prism = Lateral Surface Area + 2 × Base Area. LSA is calculated by multiplying the perimeter of the base by the height of the prism.
